summary: Measure distance from a target without its sign.
documentation: abs returns a number’s absolute value. For integers and floats this gives its nonnegative magnitude. For complex numbers it gives magnitude rather than removing a sign.
returns: The absolute value of that number.
caution: Absolute value removes direction: keep the signed difference separately if over/under target matters.
scenarios: Measure how far a cash drawer is from its expected balance.
Compare a measured size against a manufacturing target.
Show the size of a budget variance independently of its direction.
title: Measure a cash variance
problem: Input has integer fields actual and expected, in cents. Return the absolute difference between them.
goal: Use abs() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Subtract the expected amount from the actual amount, then take its magnitude.
